summary:
Saudi Arabia shut down its East-West pipeline today after drones fired from Iraq damaged it, cutting a route that can carry up to 7 million barrels of oil a day. The kingdom said the attack came from Iraqi territory, and Baghdad responded by removing a military commander and opening an investigation. The closure threatens global oil supplies at a time when markets are already tight, and officials gave no timeline for repairs.

Fighting in Yemen flared up again, with more than 900 people killed or injured and at least 5,000 families displaced in less than a week. Saudi-backed government forces and Iran-backed Houthis are clashing, and civilians are facing hunger and disease as the conflict intensifies. In the Philippines, the death toll from a ferry fire near Coron, Palawan, rose to 35, with dozens still missing. The fire started in the cargo hold and tore through the M/V June Aster in seconds; toxic fumes and heat have slowed search efforts, and the coast guard expects the toll to grow.

Tensions between Washington and Beijing are mounting ahead of the Trump-Xi summit. The U.S. says China provided satellite imagery that helped Iran locate and strike American warships, killing three troops. China's Commerce Ministry also urged the U.S. to stop spying on its AI and chip sectors, warning of retaliation after a senior CIA official defended such espionage. North Korea added to the strain by launching several short-range ballistic missiles into the sea, a day after the U.S., South Korea, and Japan ended joint military exercises that Pyongyang called provocative.

At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Chinese President Xi Jinping called on member states to play a "due role" in bringing peace to the Middle East, saying the war there has caused serious losses. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened the gathering with a push for global governance reform, asking leaders to propose ten measures to turn emerging economies from "rule-takers" into "rule-shapers." The two leaders' messages reflect a broader divide over how to handle regional crises, even as they meet under the bloc's banner.

headlines.title: Saudi Arabia shuts Hormuz bypass pipeline after drone attack from Iraq
headlines.summary: Saudi Arabia closed the East-West pipeline, which can carry 7 million barrels per day, after drones launched from Iraq damaged it. Iraq removed a military commander and opened an investigation. The shutdown threatens global oil supplies.

headlines.title: Yemen fighting re-erupts, killing or injuring 900 and displacing 5,000 families
headlines.summary: Renewed fighting between Saudi-backed government forces and Iran-backed Houthis has killed or injured more than 900 people and forced at least 5,000 families to flee in less than a week. Civilians face hunger and disease as the conflict escalates.

headlines.title: U.S. links Chinese satellite imagery to Iranian strike that killed three troops
headlines.summary: The U.S. says China provided satellite imagery that helped Iran locate and strike American warships, killing three troops. The finding deepens tensions ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.

headlines.title: Philippines ferry fire death toll rises to 35, with dozens still missing
headlines.summary: At least 35 people died after a fire tore through the M/V June Aster ferry near Coron, Palawan. Toxic fumes and heat have slowed search efforts, and officials expect the toll to grow.

headlines.title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles a day after trilateral drills end
headlines.summary: North Korea launched several short-range ballistic missiles into the sea on Saturday, a day after the U.S., South Korea and Japan concluded joint military exercises that Pyongyang called provocative.

headlines.title: Xi urges BRICS leaders to play 'due role' in Middle East peace
headlines.summary: At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Chinese President Xi Jinping called on member states to stand on the right side of history and help end the war in the Middle East, which has caused serious losses.

headlines.title: Modi pitches 'rule-takers to rule-shapers' vision at BRICS summit
headlines.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi with a call for global governance reform, asking leaders to propose 10 measures to make emerging economies 'rule-shapers' rather than 'rule-takers.'

headlines.title: China urges US to stop spying or face retaliation, cites 'gangster logic'
headlines.summary: China's Commerce Ministry called on the U.S. to immediately end espionage against Chinese companies, warning of retaliation, after a senior CIA official defended spying on China's AI and chip sectors.
